title: Power Book III: Raising Kanan: Kanan Starks Cancel Christmas On Marvin Thomas Water Off At The End of Episode 7 Of Season Five
htmlContent:
Five episodes into the final season of Power Book III: Raising Kanan, Marvin Thomas finally got his hands on the nephew he'd spent months trying not to hate. After Raqrevealed that Kanan, not Unique, was responsible for Lou-Lou's death, Marvin abandoned the composure he'd been building all season and beat Kanan to the floor of his own apartment. Only Jukebox's intervention kept the confrontation from ending in a body.

It was framed as discipline, an old-school correction from a man who had buried one brother already and wasn't prepared to lose the family's grip on the streets because of another. But anyone who has watched Kanan Stark claw his way through four seasons of loss, betrayal, and escalating violence knew that a beating, however brutal, was never going to be the end of the story. It was a debt. And Kanan doesn't let debts sit for long.

The Streets' Way of Saying It's Over

In the world Raq built and Kanan inherited, "canceling Christmas" isn't about a calendar. It's the family's own grim shorthand for a killing carried out to close a chapter for good — a phrase with roots in the same streets where Marvin himself once used it to silence a loose end earlier in the season.

By Episode 7, the show has spent an entire season teaching its audience to read that language, and it primes viewers to expect the phrase to eventually turn inward, aimed at someone wearing the family name. Kanan absorbing Marvin's beating without retaliating in the moment was never a sign of peace. It was calculation. The Kanan of Episode 7 is not the teenager the show introduced in 1991; he is a young man who has already killed his own uncle once, who has learned that hesitation is the only real danger in his line of work.

Episode 7 Brings the Family's Fracture to a Head

Titled "Penultimate Means Second to Last," Episode 7 arrives exactly where its name promises: at the edge of the end. Raq spends the hour trying to hold together a business under assault from every direction, as Stefano and Breeze continue chipping away at her operation and her allies start hedging their bets.

Marvin, still carrying the righteous anger of a man avenging his baby brother, keeps pushing to finish what he started with Kanan. But the show has spent this season slowly stripping Kanan of every reason to hold back — Lou-Lou is dead by his hand, his relationship with Raq is beyond repair, and now the uncle who once mentored him has tried to kill him.

By the episode's final act, the confrontation the season has been building toward finally lands, and Kanan closes it the only way he knows how: permanently. It's less an explosion of rage than the cold execution of a decision he'd clearly already made, consistent with a character who, according to the show's own creative team, is

"sitting with" the accountability of everything he's done and choosing, again and again, to keep doing it anyway.

What Losing Marvin Means for the Thomas Family

If Uncle Lou was, as showrunner Sascha Penn has described him, "the heart and conscience of the family," Marvin was its muscle and its last line of discipline — the one person left who could still physically check Kanan and make it stick. Removing him doesn't just cost Raq an enforcer; it removes the final adult in Kanan's orbit capable of imposing consequences on him at all.

What's left after Episode 7 is a family reduced to Raq and Jukebox, both of whom now have every reason to see Kanan not as a son or a cousin, but as a threat that got away from them. The season has always been building toward Raq and Kanan's inevitable collision, and eliminating Marvin removes the one variable that might have delayed it. There is no longer anyone standing between mother and son.

A Fitting, Brutal Escalation

What makes the moment land isn't shock value — the show has been telegraphing this outcome since the second Marvin's fists connected with Kanan's face back in Episode 5. It's the inevitability. Raising Kanan has always been a tragedy dressed up as a crime drama, a slow-motion account of exactly how the ruthless, isolated man from the original Power came to be.

Kanan closing out Marvin at the end of Episode 7 isn't a twist so much as the completion of an arc the show has been sketching since its very first season, when Raq told her son that his name was on every bullet he fired, and whatever he did after was up to him.

excerpt: Five episodes into the final season of Power Book III: Raising Kanan, Kanan Stark closes out his uncle Marvin Thomas at the end of Episode 7, a cold and inevitable act that removes the last adult capable of checking him and sets up the series' final collision with Raq.
